question.leadin: This period succeeded the Tokugawa Shogunate.
question.text: Name this period of rapid industrialization and modernization under a namesake emperor from 1869 to 1912 in Japan. The goals of the Emperor, restored to full power, were outlined in the Charter Oath.
question.clue: This period saw the creation of the breakaway Ezo republic, and its principles were outlined in the Charter Oath.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about Japanese history.
swap.text: The defeated Ishida said that he fought for the heir of this man. Known by the nicknames of "the monkey" and "the bald rat" because of his looks, his actions included the reunification of Japan and the invasion of Japan.
swap.clue: This leader, who initiated construction of Osaka Castle, led failed invasions of Korea in 1592 and 1598.

question.text: Prior to the Perry Expedition, the only Japanese port that was largely open to foreigners was this city on the southern island of Kyushu. It later became the second city to be hit with an atomic bomb during World War II.
question.clue: Trade between this city and Macau was carried out by non-American "black ships."

swap.text: The last American carrier lost in the war, the USSBismarck Sea, was lost at the battle to capturethisJapanese island. The fighting was immortalized by photographer Joe Rosenthal on Mount Suribachi.
swap.clue: Much later in the war, American forces placed a flag on Mount Suribachi during a battle on this small Japanese island.

question.text: This daimyo preceded Toyotomi Hideyoshi as the first "great unifier." He was killed in 1582 when his retainer Akechi Mitsuhide ["mit-soo-hee-day"] rebelled against him.
question.clue: In a Japanese idiom, this man "pounds the national rice cake."

swap.leadin: This battle saw the use of Portuguese arquebuses, and one side of this battle consisted of forces loyal to Toyotomi Hideyori.
swap.text: Name this battle that saw the forces of Ishida Mitsunari and Mori Terumoto defeated by those of Tokugawa Ieyasu, thereby establishing his namesake shogunate.
swap.clue: The capture of Konosu and Gifu Castles preceded this battle, whose decisive moment saw a staged round of arquebus fire signal a force of turncoats to attack the army of their initial ally Otani instead.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about the history of Christianity in Asia.
question.text: This Japanese shogunate, named after the victor at the Battle of Sekigahara, crushed the Shimabara Rebellion which was led by peasant Catholics. It also forced suspected kirishitan to step on fumi-e, or images of Jesus or Mary.
question.clue: Supporters of this dynasty lost at the Battle of Hakodate after starting the Ezo Republic during the Boshin War.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about Japanese history prior to the Meiji Restoration.
swap.text: This city was the capital of Japan until Emperor Meiji made Tokyo the capital in 1868.
swap.clue: The historic shrines and religious landmarks of this city survive today because Henry Stimson prevented it from being targeted with the atomic bomb.

question.leadin: How many capitals of Japan are there? Only one. Nevertheless, there have been many ancient capitals of Japan.
question.text: This city names a period following the Asuka and was the first Japanese capital built in the Tang Chinese style. It was also the first permanent capital of Japan, before Nagaoka.
question.clue: This was the first time when emperors adopted the title of "tenno," and other innovations during this period, such as the institution of a Council of State, were adopted in order to imitate the government at Changan and important Tang Chinese institutions.

swap.text: This first Shogunate began after Minamoto Yoritomo defeated the Tairas at the Battle of Dannoura in 1185. It was late dominated by the Hojo family.
swap.clue: Before a major battle one leader of this polity meditated to find the source of cowardice in himself, and one conflict during it occurred when the cloistered emperor Go-Toba attempted to take the throne.

question.text: After moving his capital to Kamakura, Minamoto no Yoritomo took this title, making him the military ruler of Japan. The daimyos were feudal lords subservient to holders of this title, which was later taken by Tokugawa Ieyasu.
question.clue: Ishida Mitsunari was defeated by a prominent holder of this title at the Battle of Sekigahara.

swap.leadin: Name these Japanese figures from World War II.
swap.text: After becoming commander of all Japanese naval forces in 1941, he orchestrated the attack on . He was shot down and killed in 1943, when forces used deciphered intelligence to ambush his convoy.
swap.clue: During the reign of Hirohito, this naval leader was opposed to signing the Tripartite Pact. However, he still orchestrated the surprise attack on Pearl Harbor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about aristocratic women in Heian [HAY-on] Japan.
question.text: This work, often called the world's first novel, is an important insight into Heian court life. It features the blank chapter "Vanished into the Clouds" and was written by Lady Murasaki Shikibu.
question.clue: This Heian period work, sometimes called the world's first novel, written by Lady Murasaki.

swap.leadin: The feudal title daimyo emerged from the office of shugo, which was created by this period's first leader to govern the different provinces of Japan.
swap.text: Name this period of feudal Japan ruled by the country's first shogunate founded by Minamoto no Yoritomo after he defeated the Taira clan in the Genpei war.
swap.clue: Despite the establishment of a secret police force called the Rokuhara Tandai during this period, the failure to put down akuto rebels during its later days helped contribute to the downfall of this period's government.

question.text: High-fired grey pottery called Sue was introduced by the Gaya Confederacy to Japan during this era of Japanese history, named for its keyhole-shaped tombs.
question.clue: This part of the Yamato period which transitioned to the Asuka period with the introduction of Buddhism to Japan. This Japanese era was named after large keyhole-shaped tombs.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Rokuhara tandai.
swap.text: The Rokuhara tandai were a group of civil deputies who replaced the sbugo during this shogunate, which dates from the rise of Minamoto Yoritomo and was supplanted by the Ashikaga shogunate.
swap.clue: The capital was moved from this city to Kyoto during the Kenmu Restoration.

question.leadin: Answer the following about retired emperors of Japan.
question.text: This retired emperor issued a decree in 1221 calling for the overthrow of the Hojo regent Yoshitoki to cause the Jokyu Disturbance, but Yoshitoki's son quashed this man's threat and he was exiled along with Juntoku.
question.answerHtml: Emperor <u>Go-Toba</u> [or Go-Toba-tenno or the “Later Toba” or any translation of go which means “later”]

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Jomon and Epi-Jomon cultures and peoples.
swap.text: The term "Zoku" or "Epi-" Jomon refers to the persistence of Jomon patterns in northern Japan past when this culture superseded it further south. Wet rice agriculture became dominant in this culture's namesake period.

question.leadin: Answer the following about ancient legal codes.
question.text: This 645 CE set of policies promulgated in Japan shortly after the death of Prince Shotoku established the Ritsuryo, a strange mix of Legalistic laws and Confucian rhetoric adapted for Japanese conditions.
question.clue: This set of laws promulgated during the Asuka period, which curtailed the power of regional governors and imported traditions like the equal field system from China.

swap.text: Although it is an independent corporation, Sony is associated with Sumitomo Mitsui, one of these horizontally integrated conglomerates. These conglomerates took a leading role in the Japanese economy after the postwar dissolution of the zaibatsu.
